# RiskLabs — Internal Build Spec (for parallel workers)

All code lives under ~/workspace/risklabs/. Run everything from that directory.

## 1. Dataset — data/risklabs_synthetic.csv (generated by data/generate_dataset.py)
Columns (all synthetic, clearly marked):
- `company_id` e.g. "SYN-0001"
- Financials in ₹ crore (float): `revenue`, `net_profit`, `total_assets`, `total_liabilities`,
  `total_debt`, `equity`, `current_assets`, `current_liabilities`, `operating_cash_flow`
- `report_text` (str): 3–8 sentence synthetic excerpt from an annual report / MD&A,
  containing risk language for risky firms and neutral/positive language for safe firms.
- `risk_label`: Low / Medium / High, derived from transparent documented rules
  (weighted score of ratios + text risk signals, then thresholded). Rules must be in the
  script docstring and printed when run.
- 1200 rows. Stratified-ish mix of labels.

## 2. src/features.py
- `RATIO_FEATURES = ["current_ratio","debt_to_equity","debt_to_assets","net_profit_margin","roa","roe","ocf_to_debt"]`
- `compute_ratios(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`: adds RATIO_FEATURES columns.
  Guard divide-by-zero with epsilon=1e-6.
- `compute_ratios_dict(d: dict) -> dict`: same for one company dict (used by app.py).
- Formulas: current_ratio=current_assets/current_liabilities;
  debt_to_equity=total_debt/equity; debt_to_assets=total_debt/total_assets;
  net_profit_margin=net_profit/revenue; roa=net_profit/total_assets;
  roe=net_profit/equity; ocf_to_debt=operating_cash_flow/total_debt.

## 3. src/nlp.py (CPU-light; NO large model downloads)
- `LEXICON`: dict category -> list of (phrase, weight). Categories:
  `liquidity`, `leverage`, `profitability`, `legal`, `going_concern` (positive weights),
  `positive` (negative weights, e.g. "stable demand" -1.0).
  Include phrases: liquidity concern, cash crunch, working capital pressure, default,
  debt default, declining revenue, falling margins, mounting losses, going concern,
  bankruptcy, insolvency, lawsuit, litigation, regulatory probe, auditor qualification,
  delayed payments, covenant breach, refinancing risk, etc.
- `LEXICON_FEATURES = ["lex_total","lex_liquidity","lex_leverage","lex_profitability","lex_legal","lex_going_concern","lex_positive","risk_sentence_count"]`
- `extract_lexicon_features(texts: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame`: STATELESS, fixed columns
  above. Score = sum of weights of matched phrases (case-insensitive substring on
  lowercased text); risk_sentence_count = sentences containing any positive-weight phrase.
- `class RiskTextVectorizer`: thin wrapper around sklearn TfidfVectorizer
  (max_features=500, ngram_range=(1,2), stop_words="english"); methods fit(texts),
  transform(texts)->csr matrix, get_feature_names()->list. Joblib-picklable.
- Code comment: "To use sentence-transformers embeddings instead, replace
  RiskTextVectorizer.transform with model.encode(...) — keep output 2-D numeric."

## 4. Models — models/ (written by src/train.py)
- `model_a.pkl`: joblib dump of fitted RandomForestClassifier on RATIO_FEATURES only.
- `model_b.pkl`: joblib dump of fitted RandomForestClassifier on
  RATIO_FEATURES + LEXICON_FEATURES + TF-IDF(500) — input densified via .toarray().
- `tfidf_vectorizer.pkl`: fitted RiskTextVectorizer.
- `feature_names.json`: {"financial": [...7...], "lexicon": [...8...], "tfidf": [...]}
- `median_profile.json`: median of the 9 raw financial columns (for app PDF-mode defaults).
- `metrics.json`: {"model_a": {"accuracy","precision_macro","recall_macro","f1_macro","roc_auc_ovr"},
  "model_b": {...}, "n_train": int, "n_test": int,
  "note": "Metrics on SYNTHETIC data — for pipeline validation only."}
- Label encoding: {"Low":0,"Medium":1,"High":2}; save mapping in metrics.json as label_map.

## 5. src/train.py
- Runnable as `python src/train.py` from project root.
- Stratified 80/20 split, random_state=42.
- RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1) for both models.
- Print a comparison table of accuracy/precision/recall/F1/ROC-AUC (macro, OvR) for A vs B,
  plus a note that data is synthetic. Save all artifacts above.

## 6. src/explain.py
- `FEATURE_DISPLAY`: human names, e.g. "debt_to_equity"->"Debt-to-equity ratio",
  "lex_liquidity"->"Liquidity risk language in report", tfidf terms shown as
  `word/phrase "…"`.
- `explain_prediction(model, feature_names, x_row_2d: np.ndarray, top_n=6) -> list[dict]`
  using shap.TreeExplainer; each dict: {"feature","display","value","contribution","direction"}
  where direction is "increases risk" if contribution>0 else "reduces risk".
  NOTE: contributions must be for the predicted (highest-probability) class.
- `reasons_to_text(reasons, risk_level) -> str`: 3–5 sentence plain-English paragraph.
- `risk_score_from_proba(proba) -> float`: 100*(0*pLow + 0.5*pMed + 1*pHigh).

## 7. src/pdf_parse.py
- `extract_text_from_pdf(path: str) -> str` via PyMuPDF (fitz).
- `create_sample_pdf(path: str, text: str)`: build a small PDF with fitz.
- `__main__` demo: writes data/sample_report.pdf (a synthetic risky-company report),
  extracts it, prints char count + first 400 chars.

## 8. app.py (Streamlit)
- Loads models/vectorizer/jsons with @st.cache_resource; paths relative to app.py dir.
- Sidebar mode: "Enter financial numbers" | "Upload PDF report".
- Manual: number inputs for the 9 financial fields + textarea for report excerpt (optional).
- PDF: file_uploader -> save temp -> extract_text_from_pdf -> textarea shows text (editable);
  financial numbers default to median_profile.json (shown, editable).
- On "Analyze": compute ratios + lexicon + tfidf, predict with BOTH models,
  risk score 0–100 (from proba), level = argmax.
- Show: big risk level + score; Model A vs Model B comparison table;
  category bars (liquidity/leverage/profitability/operational) as heuristic 0–100
  sub-scores derived from ratios+lexicon (label as heuristic); top SHAP reasons
  (bar chart via st.bar_chart or table); plain-English paragraph.
- Prominent disclaimer: synthetic-data prototype, educational, not financial advice.

## 9. requirements.txt — pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, streamlit, pymupdf, shap, joblib.
## 10. README.md — ASCII architecture, setup, run instructions, where real data plugs in.
## 11. VIVA.md — one-liner, research question, A-vs-B framing, 8–10 Q&A.
